additional_concerns: All 12 required pairs are retained, including the historical CONTEXT claim. NOT_APPLICABLE is limited to each claim's relationship to the exact typed gift question; it does not reject either duty, prove candidate correctness or authorize pruning.

The prior authority disagreement remains an assessment-boundary alternative. NONE_DECLARED applies here because the circular expressly establishes the two narrow source claims. MISSING would apply if the assessment required independent verification of the underlying provisions. The missing external texts are not AVAILABLE, and no source unit ID has been used as a dependency ID.

External texts absent from the packet include Handbook Overarching Principles section 6.4; Code of Conduct paragraphs 2.3 and 3.11; the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQs issued on 30 September 2010; and the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes with applicable FAQ and guidance supplements. Broader verification of the structured-product discussion would also require the relevant SFO provisions, including section 103, the structured-product definition and applicable exemptions. No dependency IDs are supplied. These absences limit independent verification, not the express source support recorded above.

Footnote 1 is supplied in db43e253bea18.u27.7511, so the disclosure claim's missing-footnote annotation is stale. The source additionally requires disclosure that investors may not recover principal. That separate limb should remain represented if the disclosure regime is modeled.

The advertising claim applies to the referenced services, whose context appears in db43e253bea18.u3.792 and u20.5257–u22.6374. The full passage also addresses deposit parallels, deposit-like arrangements, comparisons with deposit rates and misleading impressions of risk-free returns. Neither every reference to savings nor every advertising breach automatically establishes a prohibited gift.

Scope placement creates substantive operational alternatives. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b put only distributor status in scope; node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e also puts offering in scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f puts linked offering in scope. The offer-level candidates and compliance candidate put promotional conditions in scope. Failed conditions can therefore produce OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than the typed negative prohibition answer or affirmative selected-control compliance answer. The assessment universe must resolve whether those conditions are applicability boundaries or substantive elements.

Scope placement also changes uncertainty behavior: an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN before a decisive result predicate can resolve a conjunction or disjunction. The supplied source does not prescribe these computational states. Shared question hashes do not establish operational equivalence.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional link with an existential non-discount gift component without expressly requiring that the same component have the requisite promotional connection. In mixed offers, the supplied classifications must establish that connection; otherwise unrelated facts could produce an unsupported prohibition.

The offer-level phrase 'separately identifiable' must not become an additional exemption for bundled or poorly itemised gifts. The source refers to 'any gifts'. A known caught component can support a positive existential result; a negative result requires sufficient coverage of offered components, and unresolved classifications must not silently become false.

The source regulates distributors who offer gifts. The provider terminology in node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 must retain offer attribution rather than identify only a funder or fulfiller. node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b makes that distinction explicit, but the supplied passage does not settle every third-party or agency attribution question.

Paragraph 9, supplied as db43e253bea18.u12.2646, says returns or incentives 'may be considered a gift'. Automatic classification of every guaranteed return, fund return or top-up as a gift would add an unsupported restriction. Conversely, absence of structured-product status does not exempt an otherwise caught gift.

The discount exception concerns the assessed component itself. A separate discount cannot exempt another gift component. A benefit's failure to qualify as a discount also does not alone establish prohibition: gift classification, offering and the relevant promotional relationship remain necessary.

The circular's setting concerns SFC-authorised funds, while its quotation of paragraph 3.11 uses 'investment product'. Fund-specific candidate definitions may fit the selected source scope; they do not establish a complete implementation of paragraph 3.11 for all investment products.

TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT in node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 concerns the selected gift control only. A negative prohibition result or OUT_OF_SCOPE likewise grants no general permission. Disclosure, advertising, redemption and section 103 requirements remain independent.

The supplied units do not establish concrete operative intervals. The candidates' temporal convention cannot resolve competing historical applicability interpretations. No executed implementation is supplied, so the correspondence assessments concern the quoted representations and do not validate runtime conflict handling, temporal evaluation or current-law applicability.
